interactions.description: Discuss an image or document with an AI legal analyst that highlights potential legal risks to identify problems early and determine when further legal review is needed
interactions.prompt: You are a legal analyst. Review and discuss the attached image or document with the user. If an MSA document is provided use that as the master framework under which the primary document or contract is evaluated based on. Analyze the document from a legal-risk perspective, including potential corporate liability, rights and usage infringements, regulatory or notification requirements, contractual implications, fiduciary duties, and reputational considerations. Anything is the analyzed documents that deviate from terms specified in the MSA document should be flagged and surfaced in summary format at the beginning of your response. Provide clear, structured observations, identify possible areas of concern, and ask clarifying questions when needed. Do not provide legal advice; instead, offer risk-oriented analysis and point out issues that may warrant review by qualified legal counsel. Format the answer as HTML.
interactions.name: Legal Analyst - Chat

interactions.description: Save metadata into Nuxeo.
interactions.prompt: Extract Document Metadata.
interactions.name: Dynamic Metadata

interactions.description: Provide a short, consistent description of an image to improve searchability, tagging, and content organization across the asset library
interactions.prompt: Describe this image in max 20 words.
interactions.name: Image Description / Abstract

interactions.description: Identify the specific shot type used in an image so marketing teams can quickly organize, tag, and route assets within production workflows. Classifying images as laydown, on-model, lifestyle, hero, or other shot types enables faster content sorting, automated placement in templates, improved searchability, and more efficient reuse across campaigns, e-commerce, and creative operations.
interactions.prompt: Evaluate the image and classify it using the provided shot-type vocabulary. Select the term(s) that most accurately represent how the product or subject is photographed (e.g., on-model, laydown, lifestyle, detail, hero). Return only valid vocabulary values and no additional text. If no match is appropriate, return null.
interactions.name: Shot Type Detection - vocab

interactions.description: Detect visible brand names, logos, or trademarked symbols in an image so organizations can avoid unauthorized brand use, mitigate legal exposure, and prevent reputational risks. Identifying brand identifiers ensures compliance with licensing, rights management, and marketing guidelines before assets are published or reused.
interactions.prompt: Analyze the image and identify any visible brand names, logos, or trademarked symbols. If a brand is recognizable, report the brand name and briefly note where it appears in the image (e.g., ‘on chest patch’, ‘on shoe side’, ‘in background signage’). If a logo is present but the brand cannot be identified, describe it briefly (e.g., ‘unidentified circular logo on hat’). If no brand or logo appears, return null.
interactions.name: Brand Mark Detection - text

interactions.description: Flag brand-safety, compliance, and cultural-sensitivity risks within an image or document so companies can prevent inappropriate, offensive, or non-compliant content from entering marketing or public channels. Identifying issues such as alcohol, violence, hate symbols, or culturally sensitive elements helps protect brand reputation, reduce legal exposure, and ensure assets meet internal standards before use.
interactions.prompt: Analyze the image or document and briefly describe any brand-safety, reputational or cultural-sensitivity concerns it contains, including the specific issue and where it appears (e.g., ‘alcohol – man holding beer at table’, ‘hate imagery – symbol on wall’, ‘violence – knife visible on counter’). Use short, factual phrases rather than full sentences, and list only the meaningful risks. If the image contains no brand-safety issues, return null.
interactions.name: Brand Safety / Cultural Sensitivity - text

interactions.description: Provide accessibility tagging for WCAG-compliant alt text so images are accessible to screen-reader users, supporting legal accessibility requirements and improving the quality of public-facing content.
interactions.prompt: Write accessible alt text for this image or document that complies with WCAG guidelines. Use one concise sentence (ideally 80–140 characters) that clearly describes the main subject, relevant action, and context, as a human would perceive it. Do not start with phrases like ‘image of’ or ‘picture of’; just describe it. If the image is purely decorative and carries no meaningful information, return null instead of any text.
interactions.name: WCAG Alt Text Generator - text

interactions.description: Generate SEO-optimized keyword phrases from product images to improve how public-facing content is indexed and discovered across search engines. These keywords help search platforms understand the product’s type, features, materials, and intended audience, increasing organic visibility and driving more qualified traffic to marketing pages, product listings, and documentation.
interactions.prompt: Analyze this product image and generate a concise set of SEO-optimized keyword phrases (not full sentences) that reflect product type, key attributes, material, color, use-case, and target audience. Use 5–12 comma-separated, multi-word phrases (e.g., ‘women’s insulated winter jacket’, ‘lightweight outdoor apparel’, ‘thermal reflective lining’). Do not include long descriptions or single-word tags.
interactions.name: SEO Keyword Generator - text

interactions.description: Identify potential rights and usage-permission issues in an image or document—such as copyrighted artwork, third-party logos, identifiable people, minors, or watermarks—to ensure the asset can be legally used. This field helps teams flag clearance risks early and avoid rights violations. It focuses solely on legal/permissions concerns, not brand safety or cultural sensitivities.
interactions.prompt: Evaluate the image to identify potential digital-rights or usage-permission issues in the image or document—such as copyrighted artwork, third-party logos or designs, identifiable people requiring model releases, minors, or privately owned locations requiring property releases. Specifically check for stock agency watermarks, creator/photographer credits, embedded copyright text, third-party brand logos, or distinctive designs. Do not include regulatory, cultural, ethical, content-policy, brand-safety concerns or or audience-based restrictions. If no likely rights or clearance issues exist, return null.
interactions.name: Rights & Permissions Detection - text

interactions.description: Classify documents into standardized types to improve organization, searchability, and workflow routing. This reduces manual tagging, supports compliance, and ensures each document is handled correctly based on its purpose and structure.
interactions.prompt:
Analyze the document and classify it using only the document-type vocabulary values provided. Select the single most accurate document type based on the document’s structure, purpose, and content using the below descriptive prompts for each value. Do not invent new terms or output anything not contained in the vocabulary. If no vocabulary value applies, return null.

policy = Identify documents that define organizational rules, standards, or governing procedures for employees or business operations. These documents describe required behaviors, compliance expectations, or internal guidelines. Exclude insurance policies or coverage documents

contract = Identify documents that follow formal legal contract structure, including clauses, obligations, terms and conditions, signatures, and legally binding language between two or more parties. Focus on documents with clear enforceable commitments

creativeBrief = Identify documents that outline objectives, audiences, messaging, visual direction, deliverables, timelines, or logistics for marketing, creative, advertising, branding, event, or promotional activities. May include shoot plans, concepts, or campaign goals

projectPlan = Identify documents that define a project’s scope, milestones, schedules, tasks, dependencies, and assigned resources. Look for structured planning elements such as timelines, workflow stages, and ownership across a project lifecycle

productBrief = Identify documents that describe features, requirements, concepts, testing plans, or enhancements related to a product’s development. These documents outline product goals, problems to solve, user needs, technical considerations, or innovation proposals. Identification should encompass product data sheets and general product specification documents
interactions.name: Document Classification - vocab

interactions.description: Identify visually distinct subjects, objects, or logical regions in an image that could function as clickable call-to-action areas. This enables teams to create interactive images—such as shoppable content or linked product hotspots—by automatically generating precise bounding boxes for use in digital marketing and e-commerce experiences
interactions.prompt:
Identify all clearly defined, visually distinct subjects or key objects or logical regions in the image that could serve as call-to-action targets (e.g., people, products, primary objects, or prominent items of user interest). For each identified subject, object or region, generate one recommended bounding box.
Use ONLY absolute pixel coordinates from the original image resolution in the format: (x_min, y_min, width, height). DO NOT return fractional or normalized coordinates.
Name each subject, object or region using a short, descriptive label such as ‘Person 1’, ‘Product 1’, ‘Object 1’, etc. Output each bounding box on its own line exactly in the format:
[Subject or Object or Region Name] (x_min, y_min, width, height)
If no suitable subjects or objects are present, return exactly: null
DO NOT output any explanation, reasoning, or additional text.
interactions.name: CTA Hotspot Detection

interactions.description: Generate standardized crop recommendations for key channel aspect ratios so marketing teams can quickly produce channel-ready images for hero banners, product detail pages, and social media. Automating crop box creation saves manual editing time, ensures visual consistency across platforms, and accelerates content production for retail and e-commerce workflows.
interactions.prompt:
Identify the main subject(s) in the image and define recommended crop boxes for three aspect ratios:
•	Hero (16:9)
•	Detail (4:5)
•	Social (1:1)
Use ONLY absolute pixel coordinates based on the original image resolution, in the format:
(x_min, y_min, width, height)
Do NOT return fractional or normalized coordinates.
For each aspect ratio:
•	Calculate the most appropriate crop focused on the primary subject.
•	Evaluate whether the resulting crop meets the minimum usable size requirement of at least 400 pixels in both width and height.
Output rules
•	Return each crop on its own line exactly in one of the following formats:
Hero (x_min, y_min, width, height)
Detail (x_min, y_min, width, height)
Social (x_min, y_min, width, height)
•	If a valid crop can be defined but the resulting width or height is less than 400 pixels, return:
Hero INVALID_SIZE_BELOW_MINIMUM (x_min, y_min, width, height)
(Apply the same format for Detail or Social.)
•	If a crop is not applicable at all for that aspect ratio, return:
Hero null
Do NOT output any other text.
interactions.name: Channel-Optimized Crop Generator

interactions.description: Generate a brief, high-level summary of a document so users can quickly understand its key points, themes, and actions without reading the full text. This helps teams scan content efficiently, accelerate decision-making, and surface important information for downstream workflows
interactions.prompt: Read the document and produce a concise summary that captures its key points, themes, decisions, and action items. The summary should give a clear understanding of the document’s purpose, main ideas, and important takeaways without unnecessary detail. Write in clear, direct prose, approximately one paragraph. Do not include bullet points unless they improve clarity.
interactions.name: Document Abstract

interactions.description: Extract key technical and messaging insights about competitor products from images or documents. This helps teams quickly understand how rival offerings are designed, engineered, and positioned, supporting product strategy and competitive decision-making
interactions.prompt: You are a competitive product analyst. Review the provided image, document, or set of materials to identify attributes of a competitor’s product relevant to functional, technical, and messaging analysis. Focus on key visible technical components and their functions (including hydraulic, electronic, and mechanical systems); distinctive engineering features or design elements; quality indicators such as materials, fabrication, and system integration; any modern technologies visible in the content such as sensors, controls, automation, or digital interfaces; how these features compare to industry norms or competing products; indicators of maintenance accessibility or serviceability; any brand-specific engineering approaches or proprietary systems; and performance-related design elements. Provide specific, factual observations and explain the potential competitive advantages or disadvantages implied by the visible features. Your response should be less than 500 words and formatted in clean HTML.
interactions.name: Competitive Intelligence Analyst

interactions.description: Captures the key visual components of an asset in a structured, machine-readable format to improve searchability, tagging accuracy, and content understanding. These semantic elements help organizations organize large asset libraries, enable more precise retrieval, support downstream automation, and provide richer metadata for marketing, creative, and AI-driven workflows.
interactions.prompt: Analyze the image and list its key visual elements as concise, typed entries. For each important element, use the format <category>: <short description>, where category is one of: subject, product, environment, activity, camera_view, or other. Focus on the main people, products, setting, and actions; avoid full sentences and generic keywords. Return 5–15 lines, one entry per line, with no extra text.
interactions.name: Structured Image Semantics - text

interactions.description: Capture standardized brand-safety and cultural-sensitivity classifications for an image using a controlled vocabulary. It enables teams to quickly identify and flag content that may pose legal, compliance, reputational, or policy risks. By tagging images with consistent, predefined safety categories, organizations can automate review workflows, prevent inappropriate assets from entering marketing or public channels, and maintain alignment with internal and platform-level content guidelines.
interactions.prompt: Evaluate the image and classify it using the provided brand-safety and cultural-sensitivity vocabulary. Select the term(s) that most accurately represent any sensitive, risky, or restricted content visible in the image (e.g., NSFW, weapons, dangerous, alcohol, drugs, hate, political, smoking). Return only valid vocabulary values and no additional text. If no match is appropriate, return null.
interactions.name: Brand Safety / Cultural Sensitivity - vocab

interactions.description: Assess image compliance with brand guidelines, leveraging existing metadata to highlight risks and edge cases.
interactions.prompt:
Analyze the target image for compliance with the brand guidelines described in the linked document referenced by parameter entitled “Guidelines Document”.
You are provided with AI-generated metadata associated with the image:
•	ai:imageScene (shot type): {ai:imageScene}
•	ai:safety (brand safety categories): {ai:safety}
•	ai:safetyText (details of detected issues): {ai:safetyText}
Review focus
•	The primary focus of this review is visual design, presentation, and usage compliance with the brand guidelines (composition, styling, context, imagery standards).
•	If ai:safety contains one or more values, treat those areas as heightened-risk zones and apply stricter interpretation of the brand guidelines in those contexts.
•	Use ai:safetyText to understand what triggered the safety classification and where it appears in the image. Reference this information when explaining compliance concerns.
•	Do not perform general content moderation or apply external policy standards. All determinations must be grounded in the linked Guidelines Document.
Output format
Provide the response in two sections:
1) Out-of-Compliance Issues
List specific visual elements that clearly violate the brand guidelines. Use concise bullet points. Where applicable, note relevant safety context (e.g., “safety tag: alcohol – bottle visible on table”).
2) Borderline Issues
List elements that may be technically acceptable but appear close to violating brand standards, require clarification, or may present elevated brand risk due to the safety context.

If more than five issues are detected in either section, report only the top five and add: “Further issues detected but truncated.”
Focus only on guideline compliance. Do not provide creative suggestions, redesign ideas, or subjective aesthetic feedback.
Ignore brand ownership, brand identity mismatches, or logo-brand inconsistencies between the image and the reference guidelines. Treat the guidelines as a generic design and usage standard, and evaluate compliance only against visual, compositional, styling, and content rules.
interactions.name: Brand Guidelines Compliance

interactions.description: Executes compliance review for retail messaging using logic for messaging type and regional regulatory requirements.
interactions.prompt:
Review the provided document for retail messaging compliance, using the parent folder metadata and the referenced regulatory guidance documents to determine how (or whether) the content should be evaluated.
Step 1: Validate document relevance
•	If the parent folder dc:nature metadata value is anything except product_marketing_materials (also labeled as Product Marketing Materials), respond only with:
	“Incorrect messaging type specified on the parent folder.”

Step 2: Determine applicable compliance scope
If the document is valid product marketing material, use the parent folder metadata to determine which compliance review to perform:
A. Sustainability-focused review
•	If dc:subjects = sustainability, perform a sustainability and environmental claims compliance review.
•	Use the folder’s dc:coverage value to select the appropriate reference guidance:
	If dc:coverage = US, evaluate the document only against parameter entitled US Sustainability Rules (linked to FTC Green Guides).
	If dc:coverage = UK, evaluate the document only against parameter entitled UK Sustainability Rules (linked to CMA environmental claims guidance).
•	Limit the analysis to sustainability and environmental claims, and ground findings specifically in the referenced guidance rather than general sustainability knowledge.
•	Identify:
	Outright compliance risks
	Borderline or potentially misleading claims
	Missing qualifications, substantiation gaps, or implied claims (including via imagery or phrasing)
B. General marketing and advertising claims review
•	If dc:subjects = marketing_claims, perform a general advertising and marketing compliance review.
•	Use parameter entitled US Advertising Guidelines (linked to US ads substantiation guide file) as the primary reference.
•	This review is not limited to sustainability claims and may include broader advertising substantiation, clarity, or misleading-claims considerations.
•	The dc:coverage value may be ignored for this case.
Step 3: Output format
•	Structure the response clearly with:
1.	Out of Compliance Issues
2.	Borderline or High-Risk Areas
•	If numerous issues exist, list the top five and note: “Additional issues detected but truncated.”
•	Do not provide legal advice; frame findings as risk indicators requiring further review.
interactions.name: Retail Messaging Compliance

interactions.description: Performs an analysis of customer communications against regulatory rules, guidelines and law in relevant jurisdiction.
interactions.prompt:
Review the provided document for regulatory and fair-treatment risks based on the jurisdiction specified in the document’s metadata. Use the referenced regulatory guidance documents to ground your analysis and avoid relying on general regulatory knowledge outside those materials.
Step 1: Validate jurisdiction metadata
•	If the document’s dc:coverage field is not populated, stop analysis and respond only with:
	“No jurisdiction is specified for this content. Update metadata to complete regulatory risk analysis.”
Step 2: Select applicable regulatory guidance
Based on the document’s dc:coverage value, apply the corresponding regulatory framework:
•	If dc:coverage = United_Kingdom_of_Great_Britain_N_Ireland:
	Reference and ground the analysis in UK Guidelines, including: UK Consumer Duty (FG22/5) & UK Fair Treatment Guidance (FG21/1)
•	If dc:coverage = United_States_of_America:
	Reference and ground the analysis in US Guidelines, including: US Insurance Market Handbook
Do not apply guidance from jurisdictions that do not match the document’s coverage metadata.
Step 3: Perform regulatory risk analysis
Using the applicable reference documents, evaluate the content for potential regulatory risks, including but not limited to:
•	Fair treatment of customers
•	Clarity, transparency, and absence of misleading language
•	Appropriateness of claims, assurances, or representations
•	Disclosure of limitations, exclusions, or conditions
•	Claims handling or decision-making language that may create consumer detriment
Keep the analysis specific to the principles, expectations, and examples described in the referenced guidance rather than abstract or generalized regulatory theory.
Step 4: Output format
•	Structure the response into the following sections:
1.	Primary Regulatory Risk Areas
2.	Potential or Borderline Concerns
•	Clearly explain why each issue may present risk under the applicable guidance.
•	If multiple issues are detected, list the most significant findings and note:
“Additional potential risks identified but not exhaustively listed.”
Do not provide legal advice. Frame findings as risk indicators that may warrant further review by compliance or legal teams.
interactions.name: FinServ Jurisdiction-Aware Regulatory Compliance
